newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end lower on inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end lower on inflation fears.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly lower on Wednesday on fears that inflation might accelerate, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.01 pct at 103.19
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: -0.02 pct at 102.32
Volume was low at 140 million shekels with most of the trading concentrated in the Makams.

"The market was very quiet and volume was low. CPI-linked long bonds closed lower with yields touching 4.3 percent. Last month yields fell to 4.1 percent. This decline was too sharp and too fast and investors are more realistic now," said a trader at IBI Investment House.
Inflation-linked short bonds rose on fears of accelerating inflation, she said.
"The weakening of the shekel is likely to fuel inflation. Bank Hapoalim raised its CPI forcast for February to 1.1, which is relatively high," the IBI trader said.
She added that the forecast adjustment also had a negative impact on unlinked bonds and Makams, which closed lower today.
"The market was dissapointed by the minimal rate cut and investors are getting a bit worried that this is the last rate cut for the near term," said Idan Azoulay of Impact Union Portfolio Mangement.
On Monday the central bank said it was cutting its key lending rate for March by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 13.9 percent.

Dollar-linked bonds also were lower following the decline of the dollar abroad. In the local forex market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3380 shekels against 3.3390 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
